newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI tells banks to plan for more credit.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI tells banks to plan for more credit.

text.p: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor C. Rangarajan was quoted on Tuesday as saying the lendable resources of banks will expand considerably and they should thus plan for a larger credit expansion.
The government quoted Rangarajan as telling the chief executives of public sector banks on Monday that deposit growth would continue to remain strong in coming months.

It said in a statement that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told the same meeting that banks' non-performing assets (NPAs) were still extremely high and measures were needed to reduce them to sustainable levels.
The statement said the RBI governor told the bankers that while deposit growth had been strong in the current year, credit growth had been sluggish.

"He (Rangarajan) emphasised that deposit growth would continue to remain strong in the coming months and with lower cash reserve requirement and with Government borrowing programme almost completed, the lendable resources of banks would expand considerably," it quoted him as saying.
"Banks should therefore plan for a larger credit expansion," he said.

The statement quoted Chidambaram as saying that the amount of credit locked up in NPAs was nearly 400 billion rupees, "still extremely high, and measures need to be taken to reduce this hangover of the past so that the NPAs are brought down to sustainable and acceptable levels".

The statement said that "in the context of the easy liquidity situation and the favourable climate created by the latest credit policy, the Finance Minister emphasised the need for the banks to actively and aggressively compete for good credit-worthy clients".
